faq.question: Which college and teaching streams are included?
faq.answer: This is Pachaiyappa’s College in Chennai, affiliated to the University of Madras. Aided Shift I and self-financed Shift II have separate prospectuses and charges. The similarly named Kanchipuram college and other Trust institutions have separate identities.

faq.question: Can women apply?
faq.answer: The state granted the Chennai college co-educational status through its June 2026 government order. Postgraduate coeducation is also explicit in the current prospectus. Hostel access and accommodation availability remain separate from course admission.

faq.question: What are the aided bachelor’s subject requirements?
faq.answer: The BA routes use the recognised Higher Secondary pass condition. Mathematics and Physics require the science stream with both subjects. Chemistry specifies the Pure Science or stated Mathematics-stream combination. Commerce and biological degrees each have their own named subject requirements; do not assume that any stream is accepted for every award.

faq.question: What does postgraduate subject concerned as main mean?
faq.answer: The prospectus requires a three-year BA, BSc or BCom with the degree’s concerned subject as the main. Apply through the named qualifying-major route and obtain assessment of any differently titled or equivalent degree. A degree from another university requires the stated Madras provisional eligibility certificate.

faq.question: Which Computer Science entry route is covered?
faq.answer: The self-financed prospectus publishes overlapping Mathematics-only and Mathematics-or-Computer-Science clauses. This listing covers applicants who studied Higher Secondary Mathematics, which satisfies both. An applicant with Computer Science but no Mathematics should obtain a written college eligibility decision before applying.

faq.question: Are all programmes taught in Tamil or English?
faq.answer: The college’s named AISHE return establishes Tamil for the preserved BA Tamil, MA Tamil/Tamizhiyal and MA Economics routes. Confirm the current teaching and examination language directly for another award; an English subject or a No entry in an Indian-language indicator does not establish English-medium teaching.

faq.question: Does zero UG tuition mean a free programme?
faq.answer: No. The current aided prospectus explicitly waives UG tuition, while listing compulsory admission, special and university charges. The published academic total is INR 959 for BA/Commerce categories and INR 1,249 for the listed science categories. Confirm the complete applicable bill and residence costs separately.

faq.question: What are the postgraduate and self-financed tuition amounts?
faq.answer: The current aided table isolates annual MA tuition of INR 500 and MSc/MCom tuition of INR 750, with other charges additional. The current-linked self-financed table lists annual Computer Science tuition of INR 29,000 and total academic charges of INR 33,000; its undated tariff is indicative until the applicable cycle is confirmed.

faq.question: Are there SC/ST tuition concessions?
faq.answer: The current aided prospectus states a postgraduate tuition waiver for SC/ST students, subject to category verification. Other college and university charges remain payable. Application-cost concessions have separate registration conditions and should not be treated as a waiver of every programme expense.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Use the official college online portal and the exact stream prospectus. Select the programme, submit academic details and follow rank-list, counselling, interview and document-verification directions. Confirm the current notice, payable charges and payment/refund terms before accepting.

faq.question: When do classes begin?
faq.answer: Obtain the college’s next programme-specific first-teaching and reporting notice. Counselling or selection dates do not establish the start of classes, and no month from another award or stream is carried across.

faq.question: Is hostel accommodation or an overseas route guaranteed?
faq.answer: A college place does not create a right to hostel accommodation. The college describes a men’s hostel and guidance for nearby paying-guest accommodation. These listings verify domestic academic routes; overseas/NRI admission and fee categories require direct confirmation.
